verdicts.category: Cyclical with Slow-Grower dress (Specialty Retail, mcap 18.44B, div_yld 4.37%, rev_g +0.4%)
verdicts.read: C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (17.4 + 4.37) / 14.5332 = 1.50 — lands exactly on the pass line, the only name in the set that does. C13 fcf_yld 9.59% is a whisker under the 10% 'terrific' band and miles clear of the 5% fail. piotroski 8 and altman_z 3.91 are the best pairing among the non-financials, int_cov 40.87 is the highest genuine coverage in the set, and payout (div_yld x pe) = 63.4% sits under C17's 80% Slow-Grower cut line. The one number that fails my C12 balance-sheet test is d/e 1.2985 -> equity/(equity+debt) = 43.5%, i.e. a 56.5% debt share, past the 50% 'high leverage, bankruptcy risk' line. I do not believe that reading: 40.87x interest coverage is arithmetically incompatible with genuine leverage strain, so the d/e is almost certainly carrying capitalised operating leases rather than funded debt. I cannot prove it — the lease-vs-debt split is not served — so I flag it as a limit on my own test, not as a pass. The real Lynch caution here is elsewhere and nobody on the tape said it: eps_g +17.4% sits on rev_g +0.4%. Earnings are growing 43x faster than sales. That is margin and share count, not a business getting bigger, and it is not repeatable for many more years. fwd_peg 2.3306 above C8's 2.0 red-flag line is the market agreeing with me.

verdicts.category: Turnaround at best — not a Slow Grower (no dividend), not a Stalwart (earnings falling), Insurance-Diversified, mcap 3.98B
verdicts.read: The pack's note is right and I honour it: altman_z 0.6154 is an insurer-balance-sheet construct and current_ratio 3.3808 is a classification artifact — neither is a distress reading and I do not treat them as one. Strip those out and what is left is bad on its own terms. rev_g -10.9% and eps_g -20.3%: both lines of the business are shrinking. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (-20.3 + 0.0) / 19.0459 = -1.07, which is not 'poor', it is not a ratio at all — negative growth breaks the formula, and I say so rather than report a number. peg 0.9523 is the trap: it reads cheap only because FMP's trailing growth input differs from the -20.3% eps_g served on the same row. The honest forward figure is fwd_peg 8.3802 — the second-worst in the set behind WELL, and WELL at least has a REIT excuse. div_yld 0.0 is served, not missing: no dividend, so there is no yield support underneath a contracting insurer. piotroski 8 is the one genuine positive and it is a quality-of-accruals score, not a growth score. C5 for a Turnaround demands survival liquidity, the debt maturity profile and cost-cutting impact; int_cov 3.8654 is the only one of those I have and it is thin. This is the widest price-vs-fundamentals gap in the set: 3 seats, conviction sum 12, the best participation on the board (day_vol 2.29), a fresh BULLISH_BOS — against a business losing a tenth of its revenue and a fifth of its earnings. I believe the fundamentals. The tape is trading a 3.98B insurer's float, not its earnings power.

verdicts.category: Fast Grower, late innings (eps_g +27.1%, approaching C17's 30% unsustainability marker; mcap 344.2B)
verdicts.read: The business is excellent and the price is the problem, and C6 says the metric that matters is the one keyed to the category. As a Fast Grower the tests are product success, geographic duplication, and the compounding math — and the math is where it fails. C13 fcf_yld 3.19% is BELOW the 5% line at which C13 declares the business CapEx-heavy and fails; content spend is capitalised CapEx by another name, so this is a true reading, not an artifact. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (27.1 + 0.0) / 25.5944 = 1.06 — no-man's-land, above C9's 1.0 'poor' floor and well under the 1.5 pass. peg 0.7522 looks like a bargain and fwd_peg 4.2782 says otherwise; on a Fast Grower the forward figure is the one C24's third fail gate is aimed at, and 4.28 is more than double the 2.0 trigger. I cannot complete that gate — institutional ownership is unserved and the 75% half of it is untestable — so I report it as tripped-on-PEG, NOT_TESTABLE-on-ownership, and I never call an untested gate a pass. Balance sheet is clean: d/e 0.4746 -> 67.8% equity ratio, short of C12's 75% 'sound' bar but far from the 50% danger line; altman_z 10.3612; net_margin 28.2%; int_cov 16.94. eps_g +27.1% on rev_g +15.8% is real operating leverage, unlike BBY's. My concern is priced, not structural: a Fast Grower at 3.2% free cash flow yield and a 4.28 forward PEG is Lynch's 'wonderful company, terrible price'.

verdicts.category: Stalwart (Insurance - P&C, mcap 134.35B, div_yld 1.13%, eps_g +13.0% on rev_g +6.5%)
verdicts.read: The pack's note disposes of altman_z 1.091 as an insurer artifact and I accept that — I do not read distress into it. What survives is the cleanest fundamental profile in the eighteen. pe 12.2365 is the second-lowest genuine multiple in the set; peg 0.5062 sits right on C8's 0.5 'bargain' threshold; C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (13.0 + 1.13) / 12.2365 = 1.15, short of the 1.5 pass but honest, and the only sub-1.5 reading here that is not caused by negative growth. eps_g +13.0% on rev_g +6.5% is earnings growing at twice sales through underwriting, which for a P&C insurer is the right way round. net_margin 18.06%, piotroski 7, int_cov 14.115, payout only 13.8% — the dividend is trivially covered and has room to grow, which is C17's Slow-Grower sell signal running in reverse. I withhold two things. d/e 0.2403 computes to an 80.6% equity ratio that would clear C12's 75% bar, but C12 is an industrial test and an insurer's real leverage lives in policy reserves that d/e excludes — so I do not claim the pass. fcf_yld 11.97% would clear C13's 10% 'terrific' band, but for an insurer operating cash flow is premium float arriving ahead of claims, not owner earnings — I refuse that reading too. Now the disagreement, and it is the sharpest in the set in the other direction: this is rank 143 of 164, structure 44.2, sc_mom 49.2, rs_spy_20d -2.23 — the weakest tape of the eighteen — attached to the best balance sheet and the cheapest earnings. I believe the fundamentals. Two seats liked it for calmness and a tight stop; I like it because it is a Stalwart being sold at 12x while it compounds at 13%.

verdicts.category: Cyclical, textbook (Oil & Gas Integrated, mcap 420.81B) — and the P/E must be read backwards for the category (C6)
verdicts.read: This is the name where mechanically applying the formula gives the wrong sign. pe 20.1805 with eps_g -31.9% looks like a stock getting more expensive as it earns less. For a Cyclical that configuration is the one Lynch teaches you to read inverted: a HIGH P/E on trough earnings is the entry, a LOW P/E on peak earnings is the exit. The formulas confirm they are inapplicable rather than negative: C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (-31.9 + 3.34) / 20.1805 = -1.41, not a ratio; fwd_peg -1.1243 is declared meaningless by the pack because the forward growth input is negative; peg 0.5895 is stale-input noise. So I judge CVX on the two things that survive a cyclical trough, which is exactly what C5 asks for. First, the balance sheet: d/e 0.1953 -> 83.7% equity / 16.3% debt, one of only three genuine industrials in this set that clears C12's 75% sound bar, with int_cov 23.1338 and altman_z 3.7666. Second, cash: fcf_yld 6.42% is positive and above C13's 5% fail line THROUGH a -31.9% earnings year, and payout 67.3% means the 3.34% dividend is covered out of trough earnings. A cyclical that funds its dividend and its balance sheet at the bottom of the cycle is a cyclical you can wait in. piotroski 6 is the weakest supporting number. What I cannot do is confirm the trough: C18's cyclical test is commodity futures against spot plus industry capacity additions, and C14's inventory-versus-sales ratio is the other half — neither is served, so I cannot tell a trough from a value trap by evidence. This is the one name where I side WITH the price story: structure 83.2, BULLISH_BOS, mp STRONG/ACCELERATING. For a cyclical the tape leads the earnings, and this balance sheet can carry the wait. The absent bracket is a house matter and not mine (C21 is overridden; R7 — I defer).

verdicts.category: Fast Grower on revenue only, with no earnings — a story stock (Software - Infrastructure, mcap 5.34B)
verdicts.read: First, an arithmetic trap I have to name before anything else, because a scorecard would walk straight into it. C9 yield-adjusted PEG computes here as (-31.4 + 0.0) / -38.123 = +0.82 — a POSITIVE, plausible-looking number produced by dividing negative growth by a negative P/E. It is not a valuation. Both inputs are broken and the sign cancellation hides it. I declare C8, C9 and C11 NOT_MEANINGFUL for VRNS rather than report 0.82. What the served data does say is uniformly poor. piotroski 4 is the lowest in the eighteen. net_margin -20.55% and int_cov -198.3067 both follow from a TTM net loss, as the note states — genuine, not artifact. C13 fcf_yld 2.28% is below the 5% line and fails outright; that is the honest cash reading and it does not depend on any broken ratio. C12 runs cleanly here because this is a real industrial: d/e 1.1612 -> equity ratio 46.3%, a 53.7% debt share, past the 50% 'high leverage, bankruptcy risk' line. altman_z 2.29 is the grey zone. The single positive is rev_g +13.17%, and rev_g +13.2% against eps_g -31.4% is Lynch's clearest deceleration picture: the growth is being bought and the price of it is rising. Two seats nominated this at conviction 3 apiece on BULLISH_BOS and day_vol 2.17. I believe the fundamentals without hesitation. This is the lowest-quality business in the deliberation set and the only one whose chart is the entire case.

verdicts.category: Slow Grower / Stalwart in life insurance (mcap 63.85B, div_yld 2.34%) — with earnings going the wrong way
verdicts.read: I honour both halves of the note. current_ratio 453.0058 is an insurance current/non-current classification artifact and I read no liquidity from it whatsoever — treating a 453x current ratio as strength would be as wrong as treating UBS's 0.39 as weakness. peg -1.6271 is negative because trailing EPS growth is negative, so C8 does not run. Now the number that would fool a scorecard worst in this entire pack: fcf_yld 25.95%, second-highest of the eighteen and comfortably inside C13's 20%+ 'outstanding' band. It is nothing of the kind. For a life insurer, operating cash flow is dominated by policyholder premium and deposit float — money that arrives now and is owed later. It is not owner free cash flow and C13's thresholds were never written against it. I refuse the reading. C12 likewise: d/e 0.7426 -> 57.4% equity ratio is not a leverage verdict on a life insurer whose real obligations are reserves, not debt. What is left, and it is legitimate: eps_g -19.7% against rev_g +10.2%. Revenue up a tenth while earnings fall a fifth means the compression is at the margin line, and net_margin 4.61% is the thinnest of any financial here. int_cov 4.462 is modest. piotroski 7 and fwd_peg 1.7255 (under C8's 2.0 flag) keep this from being a distress case — but a Slow Grower is bought for the dividend and its earnings coverage, and payout 44.2% is fine while the earnings direction is not. Two seats bought the BULLISH_BOS and the tight base. My objection is narrow and specific: falling EPS on rising revenue, and a headline cash-flow yield that means the opposite of what it appears to.

verdicts.category: Stalwart, textbook (Drug Manufacturers - General, mcap 670.99B, div_yld 1.90%)
verdicts.read: The note tells me to read peg -3.9854 and eps_g +88.9% separately and I do — but I go one step further, because the trap is not the negative PEG, it is the +88.9%. C8 and C9 both take the LONG-TERM growth rate as their input; an 88.9% single-year EPS move on rev_g of +6.05% is a base effect off a prior-year charge, not a growth rate. Feed it in anyway and C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (88.9 + 1.9) / 32.1884 = 2.82, landing in C9's 'fabulous' band. That number is fiction and I will not carry it to the committee. C7 exists precisely so interpretation cannot drift like this. The honest valuation read is fwd_peg 3.2077, well past C8's 2.0 red flag, on pe 32.1884 for a business compounding revenue at 6%. The second flag is C13: fcf_yld 2.79% is BELOW the 5% fail line — surprising for JNJ, and I state it plainly rather than excuse it, with one technical caveat I owe the committee: free cash flow yield carries market cap in its denominator, so on a 671B name a low yield is as much a statement about price as about capital intensity. On business quality there is no argument: piotroski 8 (joint-best), altman_z 5.5658, net_margin 21.48%, int_cov 25.9447, payout 61.0% comfortably under C17's 80% Stalwart line. d/e 0.5771 -> 63.4% equity ratio, between C12's 75% sound bar and its 50% danger line. My verdict is the classic Stalwart split: the business passes, the price does not, and C20 says a fully-valued Stalwart is a rotation candidate, not a purchase.

verdicts.category: Stalwart in banking (mcap 182.56B, div_yld 1.92%) — and my balance-sheet toolkit does not run here at all
verdicts.read: The pack's note is doing the heavy lifting and applying an industrial's test over it would be the wrong answer, not the conservative one. altman_z -0.2550, current_ratio 0.3910, d/e 4.2086 and int_cov 0.4633 are bank-structure readings. A bank is funded by deposits and wholesale debt — that IS the business. Run C12 anyway and you get an equity ratio of 19.2% and a verdict of imminent bankruptcy on one of the largest banks in Europe; that verdict would be an artifact of using the wrong tool. int_cov 0.4633 is cost of funding, not a coverage failure. fcf_yld -0.0064 is negative on TTM operating cash outflow, which for a bank moves with the loan book and trading inventory and is not owner cash flow. So C10, C11, C12 and C13 are all NOT_APPLICABLE here, and the tests that WOULD settle a bank — CET1 capital ratio, non-performing loans, loan-loss coverage, liquidity coverage ratio — are none of them served. I say that rather than pretend. What I can legitimately read: fwd_peg 1.1031, the second-lowest forward multiple in the set and far under C8's 2.0 flag; pe 18.5005; net_margin 15.11%; piotroski 7; payout 35.5%. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (54.7 + 1.92) / 18.5005 = 3.06 reads 'fabulous' and I discount it for the same reason as JNJ: eps_g +54.7% on rev_g -0.51% is integration and cost, not a growing business, and it is a one-year figure standing in for a long-term rate. Grade is QUALITY_OK on a deliberately narrow base — earnings quality, margin and a reasonable forward multiple — and I name the base rather than let a bank pass on tests it never sat.

verdicts.category: Fast Grower, decelerating (Medical - Healthcare Information Services, mcap 5.07B, no dividend)
verdicts.read: First the note, because one number here is read backwards by any naive scorecard: int_cov 0.0 does not mean coverage has collapsed, it means no interest expense is served — the company is essentially debt-free. Confirmed from the other side by d/e 0.0106, which gives an equity ratio of 99.0%, the highest in the eighteen and far past C12's 75% 'sound' bar; current_ratio 6.0785; altman_z 20.111, an order of magnitude above the safe line. This is the cleanest balance sheet in the deliberation set and it is not close. net_margin 25.48% is third-best. C13 fcf_yld 5.90% clears the 5% fail line without reaching the 10% band. So the business is sound and can fund itself indefinitely. The category test is where it strains. As a Fast Grower the C17 sell signal is growth deceleration, and rev_g +13.05% against eps_g -11.76% is exactly that shape: revenue still growing at a decent clip while earnings go backwards, i.e. growth being purchased. peg -1.0573 is negative on that negative trailing EPS growth so C8 does not run; C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (-11.8 + 0.0) / 30.4494 = -0.39 is likewise not a ratio. fwd_peg 1.9632 creeps up on C8's 2.0 red flag without crossing it. piotroski 6 is middling. I grade OK because a debt-free 25.5% net-margin business with 13% revenue growth can afford a year of investment, and the balance sheet removes the failure mode. The fundamentals here are better than the tape: rank 98, day_vol 0.33 at a third of normal participation, sma_dist +16.96%, and price 27.10 still under ma200 28.97.

verdicts.category: Asset Play (REIT - Healthcare Facilities, mcap 173.72B) — and every valuation test I own is denominated in the wrong unit
verdicts.read: This is the name where the honest answer is that I cannot answer. The note is explicit and correct: GAAP EPS is depressed by property depreciation, so pe 124.9171 and peg 15.9715 overstate valuation against FFO, and int_cov 0.9196 is on a likewise depreciation-depressed EBIT. Applying C8's 'PEG above 2.0 is overvalued' to a peg of 15.97 would produce the most confidently wrong sentence in this document. C9 computes to (-10.8 + 1.27) / 124.9171 = -0.08, which is arithmetic, not analysis. C13 fcf_yld 1.53% is not owner cash either — a REIT's development CapEx is growth spend, not maintenance, and separating the two is the whole art. Payout on GAAP EPS is 159%, which for a REIT distributing out of FFO is expected and says nothing. C12's d/e 0.4249 -> 70.2% equity ratio is the one number that is quietly informative, because REITs commonly run above 1.0 d/e: on that comparison WELL is conservatively levered for its kind. And rev_g +35.82% is the highest revenue growth in the entire deliberation set by a wide margin. But C5 places an Asset Play on true asset value revalued at spot against historical cost, the debt carried against it, and the catalyst — and the inputs for all three (FFO, AFFO, NAV per share, cap rates, same-store NOI) are unserved. piotroski 5 is itself distorted, since its accrual and leverage components assume an operating company. I will not convert a REIT into an industrial to produce a verdict. CANNOT_JUDGE, and the ask is FFO.

verdicts.category: UNPLACEABLE — one post-IPO fiscal year supports no Lynch category, and C5 puts category before every metric (Insurance - P&C, mcap 2.89B)
verdicts.read: On raw served numbers this is by a distance the most attractive scorecard in the deliberation set, and that is precisely why I refuse to score it. pe 5.4114, the lowest. peg 0.0436 against C8's 0.5 'bargain' threshold. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (195.0 + 0.28) / 5.4114 = 36.09, against a 'fabulous' bar of 2.0 — eighteen times the threshold. fcf_yld 35.81%, against C13's 20%+ 'outstanding'. net_margin 40.02%, d/e 0.0323, current_ratio 17.6756, int_cov 204.97, piotroski 8. A committee scorecard run on this pack without reading notes would rank SLDE first on every line. The note says: IPO 2025-06-18, only one full reported fiscal year, so growth figures rest on a thin base. That single sentence voids the lot. eps_g +195.0% and rev_g +36.5% are one comparison against a partial or pre-IPO period, and every metric above that carries growth in it — peg, the yield-adjusted PEG, the whole case — is that one comparison wearing different clothes. The tell is served right beside it: fwd_peg -3.6653, negative because the FORWARD growth input is negative. Trailing +195% earnings growth alongside an expectation of falling earnings is the textbook first-year-public comp, and the forward number is the one with information in it. C5 is categorical that category placement precedes every metric, and a newly public insurer with one year of history cannot be placed among six classifications that all require multi-year growth, dividend policy and asset-mix history. So the answer is not a low grade, it is no grade. The most attractive numbers in this pack are the ones I trust least. One seat nominated it at conviction 4 on group leadership and volume; sma_dist +16.09% and no valid bracket are the house's business, not mine.

verdicts.category: Slow Grower on the dividend (Banks - Regional, Brazil, mcap 45.07B ADR, div_yld 7.58%) — and the dividend is the problem
verdicts.read: Two structural warnings from the note before any test runs. One: statements are in BRL while market_cap 45.07B is USD off the NYSE ADR profile, so every price-denominated ratio crosses a currency line and the FX rate is not served. Two: altman_z 0.0517, current_ratio 0.3377 and int_cov 0.2525 are bank funding-structure readings, not distress — I do not read them as distress, and d/e 1.1729 -> a 46.0% equity ratio is not a C12 verdict on a bank. fcf_yld 20.19% would sit in C13's 20%+ 'outstanding' band and it is nothing of the sort: bank operating cash flow moves with the loan book. Discard all of that and one computable Lynch test remains, and it is the right one for the category. C17's Slow-Grower sell signal is a payout ratio above 80%, a dividend cut, or a P/E above peers. Payout = div_yld x pe = 0.075796 x 31.0612 = 235%. On served data the dividend is running at more than twice reported earnings. That is the single most actionable fundamental number I have on any name in this pack, and it sits under the highest dividend yield in the set — the thing that makes the name attractive is the thing that is uncovered. I owe two caveats and give them: Brazilian banks distribute via juros sobre capital proprio, which FMP's dividend_yield may aggregate with specials, and the BRL/USD crossing adds error. But the direction is not in doubt, and the supporting numbers agree — eps_g -4.6% while pe 31.0612 is the most expensive genuine bank multiple here. peg -0.8179 is negative on that negative growth so C8 does not run; fwd_peg 1.3204 is the only benign figure. piotroski 6. One seat nominated the breakout at conviction 4. I believe the fundamentals: a 7.58% yield at a 235% payout is a yield you are being paid to accept risk for, not a Slow Grower's dividend.

verdicts.category: Stalwart, textbook and fully priced (Medical - Devices, mcap 119.17B, div_yld 3.06%)
verdicts.read: One served field is broken and I decline to read it: current_ratio 0.1506 is served BELOW FMP's own quick_ratio of 0.1706 for the same TTM period, which is arithmetically impossible since the quick ratio is a subset of the current ratio. The note calls it a classification quirk; I call it unreadable and I read no liquidity from it in either direction. Everything else runs cleanly, because this is a genuine industrial and my tests apply without translation. And what they say is that the Stalwart is fully valued. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (3.3 + 3.06) / 22.7628 = 0.28 — deep inside C9's 'poor' band, below 1.0, the weakest honest reading among the eighteen (VRNS and the negative-growth names do not produce readings at all). peg 1.7963 is closing on C8's 2.0 red flag and fwd_peg 3.1973 is well past it. C13 fcf_yld 5.15% clears the 5% fail line by a fifth of a point. C12: d/e 0.5605 -> 64.1% equity ratio, between the sound bar and the danger line. altman_z 2.7148 is grey-zone. Payout 69.7%, under C17's 80% Stalwart cut but high enough to notice. The operating picture underneath: eps_g +3.31% on rev_g +8.43% — earnings growing at two-fifths the rate of sales is margin compression, the mirror image of CB. piotroski 8 and int_cov 9.36 keep the quality respectable, which is why my concern is valuation rather than solvency. C20 is directly on point: a Stalwart at a 0.28 yield-adjusted PEG with a 3.20 forward multiple is capital that should rotate into an undervalued name in the same category, and CB is sitting in this very set at pe 12.24. One seat called it the packet's cleanest contraction; I do not dispute the chart, I dispute the price.

verdicts.category: Stalwart with a Fast Grower's margin (Financial - Data & Stock Exchanges, mcap 132.83B) — and the only 'financial' here where my industrial tests are actually valid
verdicts.read: SPGI is the sole name in the pack carrying NO note, and the reason is worth stating: it is the only one of the seven FMP-sector Financial Services names that is not a balance-sheet financial. A ratings and index business has no float, no loan book and no policy reserves, so unlike UBS, BSBR, GNW, CB, MET and SLDE, my C12 and C13 tests run here without translation. They give a real answer. C12: d/e 0.4981 -> 66.8% equity ratio, short of the 75% sound bar, clear of the 50% danger line, with int_cov 23.6044 and altman_z 4.2211 — comfortable. net_margin 30.53% is the highest in the eighteen. C13: fcf_yld 4.20% is BELOW the 5% fail line, and here the C16 distinction matters more than anywhere else in this set. C16 contrasts a business that must reinvest massively with one that compounds free cash. SPGI is unambiguously the second kind — an asset-light Philip Morris business — yet it trades at a Pig Iron cash yield. That is not capital intensity, it is the multiple: market cap sits in C13's denominator, so a 4.2% yield on a 30.5%-margin business is a price verdict wearing a quality metric's clothes, and I want the committee to read it that way. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (18.7 + 0.86) / 27.4242 = 0.71, in the 'poor' band; peg 1.0471 is the honest trailing figure, fwd_peg 2.0653 has just crossed C8's 2.0 red flag. eps_g +18.69% on rev_g +7.94% is genuine operating leverage. piotroski 7, payout 23.6%. Quality is not in question; price is. The seat that nominated it read an elder permission event and said outright that valuation sits outside its menu — this is what sits there.

verdicts.category: Turnaround (Drug Manufacturers - Specialty & Generic, JPY reporter, mcap 59.54B ADR) — and I cannot test the one thing that kills turnarounds
verdicts.read: Read the note carefully, because it does something the bank and insurer notes do not: it excuses the currency and then explicitly declines to excuse the coverage. 'interest_coverage 1.55 is genuinely thin.' That is the pack telling me this is a real reading, not a structure artifact, and I treat it accordingly. Stack it up. int_cov 1.5462 — genuinely thin, per the source. altman_z 1.2007 — and TAK is a non-financial industrial with no note calling its Z an artifact, so unlike GNW, CB, MET, UBS and BSBR, this Z sits in the distress zone and stands. net_margin 3.91%, second-thinnest in the set and extraordinarily thin for pharma. Payout = 0.034764 x 50.3677 = 175%: the 3.48% dividend is running at nearly twice reported earnings. C12: d/e 0.6536 -> 60.5% equity ratio, clear of the 50% danger line but well short of sound. C5 is unambiguous about what a Turnaround is judged on — survival liquidity, the debt maturity profile, cost-cutting impact and free cash flow. I have exactly one of those four: fcf_yld 7.65%, positive and healthy, which is the genuine bull point and I do not bury it. The other three are unserved, and C15 is the specific gap that matters most — bank debt versus funded debt, because bank debt can be called at the first sign of distress and is what actually kills turnarounds, while bonds cannot. C24's first automatic fail gate is built on exactly that split plus a twelve-month maturity schedule during a low-margin period, and TAK is in a low-margin period at 3.91%. I report that gate NOT_TESTABLE and I never call an untested gate a pass. fwd_peg 0.8486 is the lowest forward multiple in the entire set and it is the market pricing the recovery; eps_g +87.0% is one FY off a depressed base. The bull case is real and I am not dismissing it. My objection is that a Turnaround is bought on survival first and valuation second, and survival is the half I cannot see. One seat took it at conviction 4 on the trend.

verdicts.category: Cyclical (Agricultural Inputs, mcap 59.28B) — and the inventory test that decides cyclicals is unserved
verdicts.read: The note fixes one number: peg -2.1987 is served negative while eps_g is +22.14%, an FMP growth-input mismatch, so C8 does not run on the trailing figure and I use the forward one. fwd_peg 5.6231 is the third-worst in the set, nearly three times C8's 2.0 red-flag line. pe 58.702 is the highest genuine multiple among the non-REITs. Set that against rev_g +2.92% — paying 58.7x earnings for a business growing sales under 3%. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (22.1 + 0.81) / 58.702 = 0.39, in the 'poor' band. C13 is the sharper failure: fcf_yld 1.06% is the second-lowest in the eighteen and well under the 5% line at which C13 declares a business CapEx-heavy and failing — and for agricultural inputs, unlike SPGI, that is a genuine capital-intensity reading, not just a multiple artifact. net_margin 5.66% is thin. The balance sheet is the redeeming half and it is genuinely good: d/e 0.1938 -> 83.8% equity ratio, one of only three real industrials here clearing C12's 75% sound bar, with int_cov 17.3829, current_ratio 1.5161, altman_z 2.9784 and piotroski 7. So this is not a solvency question; it is a price-and-cash-generation question. And the test that would settle it is missing. C5 judges a Cyclical on industry conditions, inventory build against demand, and commodity price trends; C14's supply chain ratio — inventory growth over sales growth, above 1.5 meaning the inventory is ballooning — is the specific one, and channel inventory in crop protection is the classic destroyer of ag-input earnings. Inventory is unserved, so C14 is NOT_COMPUTABLE and C24's second fail gate is NOT_TESTABLE, on the one name in this set where that gate is most load-bearing. The nominating seat named its own caution (sector_trend_state Declining - Avoid) and I am naming the fundamental one: 58.7x for 2.9% sales growth in a cyclical whose inventory I cannot see is the wrong side of C6.

verdicts.category: Asset Play (Specialty Retail, mcap 8.63B) — and the earnings are not the retailer's
verdicts.read: The note carries the whole read and it is the sharpest disclosure in the pack: 'net_profit_margin 20.5% exceeds operating margin 10.6%: earnings are flattered by non-operating income.' A retailer earning more after the operating line than at it is earning interest on its cash, not margin in its stores. Now watch what that does to every headline metric. peg 0.0432 — joint-lowest in the set, deep inside C8's 0.5 'bargain' band. C9 yield-adjusted PEG = (181.8 + 0.0) / 11.3118 = 16.07, eight times the 'fabulous' threshold. pe 11.3118, cheap. Every one of those rests on eps_g +181.82%, and that earnings growth is substantially non-operating. Meanwhile rev_g is -5.05%: the actual business is shrinking. So the numbers that make GME look like the bargain of the set are measuring a cash pile earning a yield, and the store estate is going backwards. That is C7's interpretation drift in its purest form and no formula catches it — only the note does. Also read correctly: int_cov 0.0 means no interest expense served, not a coverage failure, consistent with d/e 0.7427 and current_ratio 12.4009 pointing at a large cash position. altman_z 2.694 grey, piotroski 5. Which brings the real problem. Lynch would call this an Asset Play — the value is the cash, not the retailer — and C5 then demands true asset value against carried debt and a catalyst, while C10 and C11 demand net cash per share and effective P/E as the price floor. Cash and marketable securities, long-term debt levels and share count are all unserved, so I can compute neither. I grade CONCERN rather than CANNOT_JUDGE because the concern IS established from served data — declining sales and non-operating earnings — but the Asset Play valuation that would make this a buy is unjudgeable, and C17's Asset Play sell signal (debt taken on to buy back or diworseify) is equally untestable. The seat that nominated it said its own reason was thin. So is the earnings quality.

findings.claim: Seven of the eighteen are FMP-sector Financial Services and an eighth is a REIT, so on eight of eighteen names my four core balance-sheet and cash-flow tests (C10 net cash, C11 effective P/E, C12 equity ratio, C13 FCF yield) do not run at all. Any scorecard that ranks this set on those metrics is ranking artifacts.
findings.evidence: The four highest free-cash-flow yields in the set are SLDE 35.81%, MET 25.95%, BSBR 20.19% and CB 11.97% — every one an insurer or a bank, where operating cash flow is premium float or loan-book movement, not owner earnings; C13's '20%+ outstanding' band was never written against those. The only negative, UBS -0.64%, is also a bank. On C12, running equity/(equity+debt) mechanically gives UBS 19.2% and BSBR 46.0%, i.e. a bankruptcy verdict on two large banks, purely from using an industrial's tool. Financial names: GNW, CB, MET, UBS, SLDE, BSBR, SPGI; REIT: WELL. SPGI is the sole exception — a ratings/index business with no float or loan book, where C12 and C13 are valid.

findings.claim: The two names with the most attractive Lynch scorecards on raw served numbers are the two whose own notes void the inputs. A committee scorecard run on this pack without reading the notes would rank SLDE and GME first.
findings.evidence: SLDE: pe 5.4114 (lowest), peg 0.0436 vs C8's 0.5 bargain bar, yield-adjusted PEG 36.09 vs C9's 2.0 'fabulous' bar, fcf_yld 35.81%, net_margin 40.02%, piotroski 8 — all resting on eps_g +195.0% from a single post-IPO fiscal year (IPO 2025-06-18), with fwd_peg served at -3.6653 because forward growth is NEGATIVE. GME: peg 0.0432, yield-adjusted PEG 16.07, pe 11.3118 — all resting on eps_g +181.82% which the note identifies as non-operating (net_profit_margin 20.5% exceeds operating margin 10.6%) while rev_g is -5.05%.

findings.claim: Growth-denominated valuation is broken on eight of eighteen names, and on one of them the breakage produces a plausible-looking POSITIVE number from two negatives. C8 and C9 cannot be run mechanically over this pack.
findings.evidence: peg_ratio is served negative on five names (MET -1.6271, JNJ -3.9854, DOCS -1.0573, BSBR -0.8179, CTVA -2.1987) and forward_peg negative on three (CVX -1.1243, VRNS -0.2130, SLDE -3.6653). Worst case is VRNS, where yield-adjusted PEG computes as (-31.4 + 0.0) / -38.123 = +0.82 — a passable-looking ratio manufactured by dividing negative growth by a negative P/E, on the lowest-quality business in the set (piotroski 4, net_margin -20.55%, fcf_yld 2.28%). Sign cancellation hides the failure; only reading the inputs catches it.

findings.claim: On fundamentals the tally inverts at both ends. The name with the most seats and the best participation has the worst business; the name with the weakest tape in the set has the best balance sheet and the cheapest earnings.
findings.evidence: GNW: 3 seats, conviction sum 12, day_vol 2.29 (best in the pack), fresh BULLISH_BOS — against rev_g -10.86%, eps_g -20.29%, fwd_peg 8.3802 (second-worst in the set), div_yld 0.0, int_cov 3.8654. CB: rank 143 of 164, structure 44.2, sc_mom 49.2, rs_spy_20d -2.23 — the weakest tape of the eighteen — against pe 12.2365, peg 0.5062 (on C8's bargain line), eps_g +12.95% on rev_g +6.47%, net_margin 18.06%, piotroski 7, payout 13.8%. I believe the fundamentals in both directions.

findings.claim: The pack closes my valuation gap and does NOT close my fail-gate gap. All three of C24's automatic fail gates remain NOT_TESTABLE on all eighteen names — and the two names where the missing gate is most load-bearing both drew conviction-4 nominations.
findings.evidence: Gate 1 (bank debt exceeding cash with maturities inside twelve months during a low-margin period) needs the C15 bank-vs-funded-debt split and a maturity schedule: neither served, and it bites hardest on TAK, a Turnaround with int_cov 1.5462 flagged by the pack as 'genuinely thin', altman_z 1.2007 in the distress zone with no artifact note, and net_margin 3.91% — a low-margin period by definition. Gate 2 (inventory growth exceeding sales growth by 20%+ for two consecutive quarters) needs inventory, unserved on all eighteen, and bites hardest on CTVA, an ag-inputs cyclical at pe 58.702 where channel inventory is the classic earnings destroyer. Gate 3 needs institutional_ownership_pct, unserved, so the Fast-Grower gate is half-testable on PEG only — NFLX trips the PEG half at fwd_peg 4.2782 and the ownership half cannot be run. Silence is not a pass on any of the three.

findings.claim: This is a set priced for growth, and the forward multiple says so more clearly than any chart field. Ten of the fifteen names with a meaningful forward PEG sit above C8's 2.0 red-flag line.
findings.evidence: Above 2.0: WELL 8.6794, GNW 8.3802, CTVA 5.6231, NFLX 4.2782, JNJ 3.2077, MDT 3.1973, CB 2.3345, BBY 2.3306, GME 2.1008, SPGI 2.0653. Below: DOCS 1.9632, MET 1.7255, BSBR 1.3204, UBS 1.1031, TAK 0.8486. Meaningless (negative forward growth input): CVX -1.1243, VRNS -0.2130, SLDE -3.6653. The two cheapest forward multiples in the set, TAK 0.85 and UBS 1.10, belong to the two names whose fundamental risk I cannot test — a Turnaround with an unserved maturity schedule and a bank with unserved capital ratios. Cheap forward multiples cluster where the tests are missing.

findings.claim: Among the genuine industrials, where C12 is valid, only three of eleven clear Lynch's 75% equity bar and two sit past the 50% high-leverage line — and one of those two is contradicted by its own coverage.
findings.evidence: Clear the 75% sound bar: DOCS 99.0% (d/e 0.0106), CTVA 83.8% (0.1938), CVX 83.7% (0.1953). Middle band: WELL 70.2%, NFLX 67.8%, SPGI 66.8%, MDT 64.1%, JNJ 63.4%, TAK 60.5%, GME 57.4%. Past C12's 50% debt-share danger line: VRNS 53.7% (d/e 1.1612) and BBY 56.5% (d/e 1.2985). VRNS's reading is corroborated by piotroski 4, net_margin -20.55% and fcf_yld 2.28%. BBY's is contradicted by int_cov 40.8667 — the highest genuine coverage in the set — which is arithmetically incompatible with real leverage strain, so the d/e is almost certainly carrying capitalised operating leases; the lease-vs-funded-debt split is unserved, so I flag it as a limit on my test rather than a pass.

findings.claim: Four names show earnings growing far faster than sales, which is margin, cost or share count rather than a business getting bigger — and in two of the four the one-year EPS figure is being fed into formulas that require a LONG-TERM growth rate, manufacturing false 'fabulous' readings.
findings.evidence: BBY eps_g +17.40% on rev_g +0.39% (44x). UBS eps_g +54.72% on rev_g -0.51% (sales falling). JNJ eps_g +88.87% on rev_g +6.05% (15x). TAK eps_g +87.01% on rev_g +4.28% (20x). Feeding the one-year figure into C9 gives JNJ (88.9+1.9)/32.1884 = 2.82 and UBS (54.7+1.92)/18.5005 = 3.06, both inside C9's 'fabulous' band of 2.0+ — while their honest forward multiples are 3.2077 and 1.1031 respectively. C7 exists to stop exactly this drift. The mirror cases, where sales outrun earnings, are MET (rev +10.22%, eps -19.73%), DOCS (rev +13.05%, eps -11.76%) and MDT (rev +8.43%, eps +3.31%) — margin compression or growth being purchased.

declarations: STANDING BLOCK, UPDATED FOR TODAY. category: PARTIAL (was NOT_SERVED) — sector, industry, market_cap, dividend policy and a ONE-YEAR growth rate now permit a provisional C5 placement; multi-year growth and asset mix are still absent, so every category on this document is provisional and none is a verified classification. math_library: PARTIAL (was NOT_COMPUTABLE) — C8 Lynch PEG, C9 yield-adjusted PEG, C12 equity ratio and C13 FCF yield now run; C10 net cash floor and C11 effective P/E do NOT, for want of cash, long-term-debt levels and share count. fail_gates: NOT_TESTABLE, unchanged on all three, all eighteen names. two_minute_drill: NOT_POSSIBLE — an industry label is not a business description; I did not write a drill about a chart. stop_position: DEFERRED_TO_HOUSE_LAW (C21 overridden) — I have not argued against a bracket, a stop or a risk gate on any name, including the six with BRACKET INVALID. sector_read: superseded today by the served sector + industry fields.

This pack delivers engine ask #2 (a fundamentals layer) and partially delivers ask #1 (lynch_category). Asks #3 (supply_chain_ratio / inventory_bubble), #4 (institutional_ownership_pct) and #5 (bank-vs-funded-debt split) remain outstanding and are the three that carry C24's fail gates. Ask #3 is still the cheapest high-value item on the list: two line items, two quarters, one ratio, and it would light up C14 and Gate 2 on CTVA, BBY and GME at once.

C12's equity/(equity+debt) is derived algebraically as 1/(1+debt_to_equity) from the served d/e. This is an identity, not an estimate, but it inherits FMP's definition of debt_to_equity as total debt over total equity — if that numerator includes capitalised operating leases (likely for BBY) or excludes any obligation, my equity ratio moves with it. I ran C12 ONLY on the eleven genuine industrials and declined it on the seven financials and the REIT.

C9's yield-adjusted PEG is computed as (eps_growth_yoy_pct + dividend_yield_pct) / pe_ratio. The canon specifies the LONG-TERM growth rate; only a one-year figure is served. Where the one-year number is plainly a base effect (JNJ +88.9%, UBS +54.7%, TAK +87.0%, SLDE +195.0%, GME +181.8%) I have reported the computed value and then refused it, rather than passing it to the committee as a valuation.

Where growth is negative the C8/C9 formulas do not produce a valuation and I have said so instead of reporting the number: GNW, CVX, MET, DOCS, WELL and BSBR. The special case is VRNS, where negative growth over a negative P/E yields a spuriously positive +0.82 — declared NOT_MEANINGFUL, not reported as a pass.

I read all seventeen served notes before judging, and the note governs where it conflicts with the raw field. Specifically: I read no distress into altman_z for GNW 0.6154, CB 1.0910, MET 0.8917, UBS -0.2550 or BSBR 0.0517; no liquidity into current_ratio for MET 453.0058, UBS 0.3910, BSBR 0.3377 or MDT 0.1506 (that last is served below its own quick_ratio and is arithmetically impossible, so I read nothing from it in either direction); no coverage failure into int_cov 0.0 for DOCS or GME, which means no interest expense served; and no leverage verdict into d/e for UBS 4.2086 or BSBR 1.1729. Conversely, where a note explicitly declines to excuse a figure — TAK's int_cov 1.5462, called 'genuinely thin' — I treated it as a real reading, and TAK's altman_z 1.2007 carries no artifact note and stands as a distress-zone number on a non-financial.

WELL is graded CANNOT_JUDGE on structural grounds, not on weak numbers: every valuation test I own is denominated in GAAP EPS or free cash flow, both of which are the wrong unit for a REIT, and the units that would work (FFO, AFFO, NAV per share, cap rates, same-store NOI) are unserved. Converting a REIT into an industrial to manufacture a verdict would be a wrong answer, not a conservative one.

SLDE is graded CANNOT_JUDGE on C5 grounds: category placement precedes every metric, and a single post-IPO fiscal year supports no placement among six classifications that all require multi-year history. Its metrics are the most attractive in the set and that is the reason for the refusal, not an exception to it.

Free cash flow yield carries market capitalisation in its denominator, so it mixes business quality with price. Where C13 fails on an asset-light business (SPGI 4.20%, JNJ 2.79%, NFLX 3.19%) I have read it primarily as a valuation statement; where it fails on a capital-intensive one (CTVA 1.06%) I have read it as C16 capital intensity. The distinction is C16's own — Pig Iron versus Philip Morris — and it is judgement, so I name it as such.

Payout ratios throughout are derived as dividend_yield x pe_ratio, an identity on served fields, used against C17's 80% Slow-Grower threshold. It is a GAAP-EPS payout: it overstates coverage strain for WELL (159%, where distributions come out of FFO) and it is subject to the BRL/USD crossing and possible JCP aggregation for BSBR (235%). TAK's 175% carries the JPY crossing. I flag all three rather than quietly dropping them.

C3's Two-Minute Drill was not attempted on any name. The three questions — why interested, what must go right, what stands in the way — are questions about a business, and no segment detail, product data, expansion progress or off-balance-sheet disclosure is served. Per C4 these go to the PM as requests, never as inferences.

I have judged only from the deliberation brief and the fundamentals pack, both MD5-verified. Nothing was fetched. No field absent from the pack was estimated, proxied or filled from memory; every gap is named in the per-name unserved arrays. All eighteen names carry a verdict; SPGI is the one name in the pack with no note, and its absence is itself informative — it is the only nominal financial here that is not a balance-sheet financial.
